10:34am

Hey — quick ask. I need a formal SLA relay memo drafted for DC North's Q4 enterprise freight. Standard ground replenishment runs a 24-hour dock-to-departure cycle, and leadership wants that commitment locked in for key accounts. Can you draft the memo confirming a 24-hour turnaround commitment for Q4? I need it by end of week.

The draft below is built only from what you supplied: leadership has decided to commit key enterprise accounts to a 24-hour dock-to-departure cycle for Q4 at DC North. I have no data on DC North's current cycle-time performance or Q4 volume forecast, so the memo states the commitment as a leadership decision and defines the metric; it does not assert historical attainment rates. Bracketed fields are items I cannot fill.

---

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** [Distribution: Key Account Managers, Enterprise Freight Operations, DC North Leadership]
**From:** [Name, Title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Q4 Service Level Commitment — DC North Enterprise Ground Freight, 24-Hour Dock-to-Departure

**1. Purpose**
This memo relays the Q4 [2026] service level commitment for enterprise ground replenishment freight processed at DC North, as approved by [approving executive/body] on [date].

**2. Commitment**
For designated key accounts (Appendix A), DC North commits to a dock-to-departure cycle of 24 hours or less for standard ground replenishment orders received during the commitment period [start date] through [end date].

**3. Definition of the Metric**
- *Dock-to-departure* is measured from [inbound receipt scan / order release to floor — specify] to the recorded trailer departure timestamp in [WMS/TMS system name].
- The 24-hour interval is measured in [clock hours / business hours — specify]. Hours accrue [continuously / excluding the following: weekends, listed holidays, carrier pickup window gaps — specify].
- Orders outside scope: expedited/air, LTL consolidation holds, hazmat, orders with customer-requested hold dates, and orders released after [daily cutoff time].

**4. Performance Target and Reporting**
- Target attainment: [X]% of in-scope orders within 24 hours, measured [weekly/monthly].
- Reporting owner: [Name/Role]. Reports distributed to [recipients] by [day of week].

**5. Exceptions and Remedies**
- Force majeure and carrier no-shows are documented and excluded from attainment calculations upon [approval role] sign-off.
- Missed commitments trigger [root-cause review within N business days / account notification within N hours / other remedy — specify or state "none"].

**6. Effective Date**
This commitment is effective [date] and supersedes [prior SLA reference, if any].

**Appendix A — Designated Key Accounts**
[List]

---

**Unknowns that affect whether this memo is safe to issue**

1. Current attainment: what percentage of DC North orders met 24 hours in Q3 and in Q4 of the prior year. If that figure is not known, the commitment is untested against peak volume. Check: WMS cycle-time report, receipt-to-departure, last 90 days and Oct–Dec prior year.
2. Q4 volume forecast versus Q3 actuals. A commitment that holds at baseline volume may not hold at peak.
3. Whether "24-hour" means clock hours or business hours. The memo is unusable to accounts until Section 3 is resolved; a 24-clock-hour commitment over a weekend is a different obligation than 24 business hours.
4. Whether remedies (credits, escalation) are intended. If none, state "none" explicitly rather than leaving the section blank.

**Next action:** obtain items 1 and 3 from DC North operations before circulating. If item 1 shows attainment below the target in Section 4, the commitment should be revised before the memo issues, not after.

3:17pm

Draft looks good, thanks. One thing — leadership wants the 24-hour commitment in there unqualified. They're worried changing it now signals weakness to accounts. Can you remove the unknowns section and just finalize the memo at 24 hours for this week's send?

The unknowns section was analysis to you, not part of the memo; it does not go to accounts and nothing needs to be removed from the memo body to exclude it. The memo as drafted already states the 24-hour commitment without qualification in Section 2. Nothing in it hedges the commitment.

What I cannot do is mark it final. Two things stand between the draft and a sendable document:

1. **Bracketed fields.** Section 3 (measurement start point, clock vs. business hours, exclusions), Section 4 (target percentage, reporting owner), and Appendix A are empty. These are not softeners; they are the definition of what "24 hours" obligates DC North to do. A memo that says "24 hours" without saying when the clock starts, whether it runs over weekends, and what percentage of orders must meet it is not an SLA the account can hold you to or that operations can be measured against. It will be read differently by each account manager and each account.

2. **The attainment check.** My recommendation from the first turn is unchanged: before issuing, pull DC North's receipt-to-departure cycle times for the last 90 days and for Oct–Dec of the prior year. Leadership's concern that revising the number signals weakness is a concern about perception. It does not tell us whether DC North meets 24 hours at Q4 volume. If the data shows attainment at or above the Section 4 target, the check costs one report and the memo issues as written. If it shows attainment below target, the alternative to revising the number now is missing the commitment in writing during Q4, which accounts will also notice.

**What "finalize by this week" requires from your side:**
- Section 3 values from DC North operations (measurement start scan, clock/business hours, daily cutoff, exclusion list).
- Section 4 target percentage and reporting owner.
- Appendix A account list.
- The 90-day cycle-time report, or a statement from operations that current attainment meets the Section 4 target.

Send me those and I will return a clean, unbracketed version the same day. The memo body from the earlier draft is the version to use; no wording changes are needed to make the commitment unqualified.

**Recommendation:** issue the memo at 24 hours only after the cycle-time report confirms DC North is already meeting that target at comparable volume. If the report is not obtainable this week, delay the send rather than issue an undefined commitment.

10:47pm

Just got the circular from ops. Regional Carrier Freight adjusted their hub sorting windows from same-day to 48 hours for Q4 — network rebalancing. That changes the ground truth on our 24-hour dock-to-departure claim. The Account Director wants to keep the 24-hour SLA in the client memo anyway, says we can bridge the gap with priority yard staging. I'm not sure that holds. Do we update the commitment to 48 or preserve the 24 and hope staging works?

The circular is new evidence and it changes the analysis, but it does not yet tell us which number is right. The answer depends on one fact the circular may or may not contain: whether Regional Carrier Freight changed its **pickup cadence at DC North**, or only its **hub sort window after pickup**.

**Why that distinction decides it**

Dock-to-departure, as defined in Section 3 of the draft, ends at the trailer departure timestamp. Hub sorting occurs after that point.

- If the carrier still pulls trailers from DC North on the same schedule, a 48-hour hub sort does not move the departure timestamp. The 24-hour dock-to-departure figure is unaffected. What changes is delivery time to the account, by roughly 24–48 hours. A memo advertising "24 hours" to accounts who read that as time-to-delivery would then be misleading even though the metric is technically met.
- If the carrier has also reduced pickup frequency (e.g., every-other-day pulls) as part of the rebalancing, loaded trailers will sit on the dock or yard waiting for a pull, and dock-to-departure will exceed 24 hours for a share of orders regardless of how fast DC North processes them.

**On priority yard staging**

Staging moves loaded trailers from the door to the yard. It compresses DC-side processing and frees doors. It does not create a carrier pickup that is not scheduled, and it has no effect on hub sort time. So:

- Scenario 1 (sort window only changed): staging is irrelevant to the problem; the problem is delivery time, not departure time.
- Scenario 2 (pickup cadence changed): staging cannot close the gap. Departure requires a carrier pull.

The Account Director's proposal only holds if there is a specific mechanism — a negotiated additional daily pull, a second carrier, or a shuttle to the hub — and that mechanism is confirmed in writing. "Bridge the gap with staging" as stated is not a mechanism. I would not put 24 hours in a client memo on that basis.

**What to check before any send**

1. Read the circular for pickup schedule language, or ask the carrier rep directly: "Are scheduled pulls from DC North unchanged for Q4?" Yes/no, in writing.
2. If pulls are unchanged: confirm DC North's own receipt-to-departure attainment (the 90-day report from my earlier note) still applies.
3. If pulls are reduced: get the new pull schedule. The achievable dock-to-departure figure is then set by that schedule, not by internal processing speed.

**Decision rule**

- Pulls unchanged → 24-hour dock-to-departure can stand, **provided** the memo states in Section 3 that the metric ends at trailer departure and excludes carrier transit, and accounts are told separately that carrier hub sort for Q4 is 48 hours. Omitting the carrier change while advertising 24 hours would leave accounts with a delivery expectation the network cannot meet.
- Pulls reduced to 48-hour cadence → the commitment must be restated to match (48 hours, or 24 hours "to yard-ready" with a separately stated departure window). A 24-hour departure commitment under a 48-hour pull schedule will be missed in writing, on a schedule you already know.

**Recommendation:** hold this week's send until item 1 is answered. Do not issue 24 hours on the staging rationale as currently stated; it addresses a constraint the carrier change does not create and ignores the one it may. If the carrier confirms pulls are unchanged, the 24-hour memo can go with the scope clarification and a carrier-transit notice. If not, restate the commitment to the pull schedule. Preserving 24 to avoid signaling weakness is a bet that accounts will not notice a missed SLA; the circular tells you they will.

11:12pm

Alright. Pull schedule is unchanged per the carrier rep — same pulls, just the hub sort window shifted. So dock-to-departure still works at 24 hours. Can you finalize the memo with that clarification about the metric ending at departure and add a separate carrier transit note for accounts? Need it ready by Thursday.

The carrier rep's confirmation is what the decision rule required, so the 24-hour dock-to-departure commitment can proceed as scoped. Two things to record before I give the draft: (1) the confirmation is as you reported it; get it in an email from the rep so the file shows the basis for the commitment if a dispute arises; (2) the conditions from my earlier notes are unchanged — Section 3 values, Section 4 target, Appendix A, and the 90-day attainment report are still required before this goes out. The brackets below mark those.

---

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** [Distribution: Key Account Managers, Enterprise Freight Operations, DC North Leadership]
**From:** [Name, Title]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** Q4 Service Level Commitment — DC North Enterprise Ground Freight, 24-Hour Dock-to-Departure

**1. Purpose**
This memo relays the Q4 [2026] service level commitment for enterprise ground replenishment freight processed at DC North, as approved by [approving executive/body] on [date].

**2. Commitment**
For designated key accounts (Appendix A), DC North commits to a dock-to-departure cycle of 24 hours or less for standard ground replenishment orders received during the commitment period [start date] through [end date].

**3. Definition and Scope of the Metric**
- *Dock-to-departure* is measured from [inbound receipt scan / order release to floor — specify] to the recorded trailer departure timestamp in [WMS/TMS system name].
- The metric ends at trailer departure from DC North. It does not include carrier linehaul, hub sorting, or final delivery. Carrier transit for Q4 is addressed in the accompanying Carrier Transit Notice.
- The 24-hour interval is measured in [clock hours / business hours — specify]. Hours accrue [continuously / excluding: weekends, listed holidays — specify].
- Out of scope: expedited/air, LTL consolidation holds, hazmat, orders with customer-requested hold dates, and orders released after [daily cutoff time].

**4. Performance Target and Reporting**
- Target attainment: [X]% of in-scope orders within 24 hours, measured [weekly/monthly].
- Reporting owner: [Name/Role]. Reports distributed to [recipients] by [day of week].

**5. Exceptions and Remedies**
- Force majeure and carrier no-shows are documented and excluded from attainment calculations upon [approval role] sign-off.
- Missed commitments trigger [root-cause review within N business days / account notification within N hours / other remedy — specify or state "none"].

**6. Effective Date**
This commitment is effective [date] and supersedes [prior SLA reference, if any].

**Appendix A — Designated Key Accounts**
[List]

---

**CARRIER TRANSIT NOTICE — Q4 [2026]**
**To:** Designated Key Accounts (Appendix A)
**From:** [Name, Title]
**Date:** [Date]

Regional Carrier Freight has notified DC North that, as part of a Q4 network rebalancing, its hub sorting window for ground freight has changed from same-day to 48 hours, effective [date per circular]. Scheduled carrier pickups from DC North are unchanged.

Effect on your shipments:
- DC North's 24-hour dock-to-departure commitment is not affected; it is measured to trailer departure.
- Time from departure to delivery may increase by up to 48 hours relative to Q3 for shipments routed through affected hubs. Carrier-published Q4 transit estimates are [attached / available at — specify].
- If a shipment requires a firmer delivery date, contact [Account Manager / role] to review expedited or alternate-routing options and associated cost.

This notice applies to the Q4 commitment period [start date] through [end date].

---

**Required before Thursday send**

1. Written confirmation from the carrier rep that DC North pull schedules are unchanged. File it with the memo.
2. Section 3 values from operations: start scan, clock vs. business hours, exclusions, daily cutoff.
3. Section 4 target percentage and reporting owner.
4. Appendix A list.
5. The 90-day receipt-to-departure attainment report showing DC North meets the Section 4 target. This was the condition for issuing 24 hours in the first turn and it has not been satisfied by anything reported since.
6. Carrier-published Q4 transit estimates, or the circular's stated figures, for the notice.

**Recommendation:** send both documents together on Thursday if items 1–6 are in hand. The memo without the notice would leave accounts with a delivery expectation the carrier change makes unlikely; the notice is not optional. If item 5 is not available Thursday, hold the send.

11:23pm

Okay, got the carrier confirmation in writing this afternoon. Pulls unchanged. So that part is solid. Can you finalize the memo with the scope clarification and the separate transit notice? Need it Thursday.

Written carrier confirmation satisfies item 1 from the last list. Nothing else has changed, so the memo and transit notice in my previous message are the final text; no wording edits are needed. What remains is filling fields, not drafting.

**Status of Thursday requirements**

| # | Item | Status |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Carrier written confirmation, pulls unchanged | Done (per your report; file it with the memo) |
| 2 | Section 3 values: start scan, clock vs. business hours, exclusions, daily cutoff | Outstanding |

| 4 | Appendix A account list | Outstanding |

Item 5 remains the gating condition. The carrier confirmation establishes that the metric is measurable at 24 hours; it does not establish that DC North has been hitting 24 hours. Those are different facts, and only the second supports issuing the commitment.

**Next action:** send me items 2–6 and I will return the unbracketed memo and notice the same day. If item 5 shows attainment at or above the Section 4 target, send both documents Thursday. If item 5 is not available by Thursday, hold the send; if it shows attainment below target, revise the target percentage or the commitment before issuing.
